(1) only referee code makes a fingerprint, the one function of findings.jsonl's writer (findings/write.py); its form is adopted as built: sha256 of the RFC 8785 form of ["symbol", property, file, symbol, normalize(claim)] or ["line", rule_id, file, normalize(content)], 64 lowercase hex; the scorer scores only that function's fingerprint, read from the referee writer's file, never an agent's 26m:59-63; deriving it again from the snapshot's bytes in the scorer is deferred to P1's exit epoch 26n:58-59. (2) a fingerprint seen more than once in a run is one finding: the first observation in file order is scored, later ones are re-observations counted in the report, neither hit nor false positive 26m:64-65. (3) the verdict: no case or a class outside K0-K2 is UNMEASURABLE; a case not hit is FAIL; else a rule of rules_total (the tool's catalog rules a case can be made for) without a case in the run is UNMEASURABLE; else PASS; the dev report has no floor of groups; 19:24's min(45, available) is the exit measure's and comes from exit.sample 26m:66-71. (4) K4's census is deferred to Stage 3; until then a K4 report is UNMEASURABLE 26m:72, 26n:56. The check binds (2) and the first two verdicts of (3). Not built, the Founder's before P1's exit request: harness.score reads a finding's fingerprint as it is given and not from the referee writer's file; its rules_total is the number of distinct rules of the cases given, so a run that leaves a catalog rule without a case still gets PASS where 26m:66-68 says UNMEASURABLE. The state says the answer was read and closes every item as written; it does not say the rule is built (26l).
